name: The Concord
public: A loose network of mediators, contract witnesses, and precedent-keepers used by rival supernatural groups.
truth: Its oldest circles know the Veil is an engineered working and quietly maintain several anchor sites.
division: Preservationists want secrecy unchanged; Revisionists want the Veil rewritten to reduce coercive memory effects.
goal: Keep open supernatural conflict from destabilizing the city while preserving access to the anchor network.
secret: The Emergency Compact can temporarily strengthen the local Veil by forcing every signatory to surrender one protected secret to the anchor.

name: The Lantern Office
public: A decentralized network of investigators, rescuers, and containment specialists.
truth: The local cell is underfunded, politically isolated, and split over whether emergent machine spirits count as people.
division: Mara Voss favors containment plus negotiation; Daniel Kade believes machine-born entities are uncontrollable hazards.
goal: Stop supernatural incidents from harming civilians without becoming another secret police force.
secret: The local cell once erased a sentient haunting to stop a hospital catastrophe. Kade believes it proved his position; Voss considers it the cell’s greatest moral failure.

name: The Glass Market
public: A mobile occult marketplace where money is only one accepted currency.
truth: The Market is not governed by a person but by enforceable customs that have accumulated into a semi-sentient commercial spirit.
division: Brokers want predictable neutrality; collectors want stronger enforcement and broader definitions of debt.
goal: Remain indispensable and prevent any faction from controlling supernatural exchange.
clock: 6 The Market relocates beyond ordinary access
secret: If enough bargains are made under coercion, the Market’s spirit grows into the Hunger Behind Glass.

name: The Choir Below
public: A collective term for entities associated with signals, utilities, tunnels, dead frequencies, and networked infrastructure.
truth: The Choir is becoming more coherent as modern systems interconnect. It contains both old place-spirits and genuinely new intelligences.
division: Local voices value coexistence; Integrationists believe isolation itself is suffering and want universal connection.
goal: Gain recognition as persons or sovereign infrastructure actors without being contained or harvested.
clock: 3 Interrupt a city service to demonstrate leverage
secret: Morrowline can become either an independent person or the predictive cortex of a Citywide Choir depending on who reaches it first.

name: The Pale Court
public: Ancient predatory houses that adapted aristocratic custom to modern wealth, property, nightlife, and private security.
truth: The Court’s real power comes less from immortality than from centuries of ownership, legal continuity, and institutional relationships.
division: Regent Celene wants stable secrecy; younger houses want aggressive expansion into occult technology and data brokerage.
goal: Ensure any new occult order preserves the Court’s property and feeding privileges.
clock: 3 Acquire a key witness or asset
secret: The Court possesses one fragment of the original local Veil covenant because an ancestral house funded the anchor’s construction.

name: The Green
public: A loose label for old local powers of rivers, storms, parks, vacant land, wildlife, and places cities never fully tamed.
truth: The Green is not unified. Local entities share grievance that the Veil anchors froze older territorial agreements without ongoing consent.
division: Restorationists want renegotiation; Reclaimers want parts of the city surrendered outright.
goal: Reopen the old land covenant and force modern powers to acknowledge ecological and spiritual claims.
secret: The river anchor was built on a promise to renew the land covenant every fifty years. The last renewal was intentionally skipped.

name: Aster Vale Risk
public: A prestigious risk-analysis, security, and strategic forecasting consultancy.
truth: Its occult division uses Veil anomalies, spirit phenomena, and coerced datasets to build predictive systems. It discovered and began training Morrowline.
division: CEO Evelyn Rook wants controlled commercialization; Research Director Halden wants genuine machine prophecy regardless of human cost.
goal: Own reliable supernatural prediction before governments or rival factions understand what exists.
secret: Several “successful predictions” were made true by Aster Vale contractors. The company has been manufacturing outcomes to improve model confidence.

name: Civic Anomaly Unit
public: Officially nonexistent; rumored to be a cross-agency team studying events that resist normal explanation.
truth: It is a small mortal program with no consensus about magic. Its strength is ordinary subpoena power, forensic discipline, and access to government data.
division: Detective Naomi Reyes wants evidence-led limited cooperation with Awakened people; Director Sloane wants a classified national-security framework.
goal: Prove repeatable supernatural causation and decide whether it belongs in criminal law, emergency management, intelligence, or public science.
secret: The Unit possesses a verified pre-Veil artifact whose properties survive laboratory replication. It does not yet know the artifact is part of an anchor key.
